summary: A letter to TIP users from BBN about a revised TIP User's Guide in loose-leaf form. It lists new commands, including binary input and output, linefeed handling, wild device settings, and magnetic tape commands that apply to TIPs with the tape option. The letter explains the changes.

eli5.summary: A letter telling people who use a dial-in box that its instruction book has been updated, and showing the new buttons they can use.

questions: what is a tip on the arpanet
subtitle: BBN tells TIP users about new commands, buffer limits, echo changes and where to report problems.

tldr.problem: TIP users needed to know what changed in the TIP program and how to get help, with buffer space for terminal devices steadily shrinking.
tldr.mechanism: David Walden's letter lists the new TIP commands, the planned ECHO command changes, the nominal buffer sizes and how to report problems to BBN's Network Control Center.
tldr.outcome: It is an informal notice of coming changes, with no formal protocol specification.

today: The unit metadata lists this RFC's status as Unknown, and no RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it. The letter describes changes as planned or in progress as of July 11, 1972.

sections.title: New Commands and the Revised Guide
sections.content:
BBN will send a revised TIP User's Guide in loose-leaf format, with descriptions of new commands and an alphabetical list of all TIP commands in Appendix B. The new commands include binary input and output start and end, @CLEAR DEVICE WILD, @INSERT LINEFEED, @SEND COMMAND and a family of @MAG commands for magnetic tape. The MAG commands matter only to TIPs with the magnetic tape option.

A TIP system with these commands has been in operation since late June. The letter counts eleven TIPs in the ARPA Network and says another will soon be installed at CCA.
sections.eli5: The instruction book for the dial-in box got new pages, because the box learned new tricks, like handling tape machines.

sections.title: Status, Support and Buffers
sections.content:
New TIP versions are loaded when no one is using a TIP. In future, a status message with the version number will be added to the HELLO at logon, and the word NEWS signals that @NEWS should be read. Problems go to BBN's always-manned Network Control Center rather than to the Host being used.

Only about 2500 characters of buffers are available for the terminal devices, shared by 63 devices. Each device has one input buffer and two output buffers, averaging about 13 characters each. Nominal sizes range from 60 input and 56 output characters for devices 1 to 3 down to 6 and 6 for devices 33 to 63. Space is slowly shrinking, and BBN suggests more core or modularizing the program.
sections.eli5: The box has only a little memory for each keyboard, like a few seconds of talking. Faster devices get more room, and the room is slowly getting smaller.

sections.title: Changes to Echoing
sections.content:
BBN will remove ECHO ALL, ECHO HALFDUPLEX and ECHO NONE, slightly change ECHO REMOTE and ECHO LOCAL, and add PHYSICAL HALFDUPLEX and PHYSICAL FULLDUPLEX. Known physical half-duplex devices such as IBM 2741s start in that mode; all others start as physical full-duplex with local echo.

When the TIP receives Telnet ECHO (code 132) or NO ECHO (code 131), it follows a table of rules that depends on its mode, sending ECHO or NO ECHO to the server or doing nothing. When a connection breaks, physical full-duplex devices revert to virtual half-duplex. The letter admits that @@ is still often echoed incorrectly.
sections.eli5: The box is getting a simpler set of switches for who shows your typing, you or the faraway computer, and it resets them when the call ends.

sections.title: Planned and Possible Work
sections.content:
Planned command changes: PROTOCOL TO LOGIN is removed in favor of LOGIN, which will take a Host number parameter so HOST is not needed. Work in progress includes returning captured devices when a terminal hangs up, output to high speed devices, working 202C modems, improvements to the magnetic tape option and investigating reports that the TIP loses an allocate.

Under consideration are lower case for Model 33 Teletypes and a way for users to get TIP or device status. Each change will be announced via NEWS, and Walden invites suggestions, especially ones that need no memory.
sections.eli5: The writer lists bugs he is fixing and ideas he is thinking about, and asks readers for suggestions.
